A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a kind of deep network built for data laid out in a grid, most often images. Instead of connecting every input pixel to every [[Neuron]], it slides a small grid of numbers called a [[Convolution|filter]] across the image. At each position it computes one number that says how strongly the patch matches the filter's pattern, such as a vertical edge. The collected numbers form a feature map.

Because the same filter is reused everywhere, the network needs far fewer weights and can spot a pattern wherever it appears. After each convolution, an [[Activation Function|activation function]] adds non-linearity, and [[Pooling]] shrinks the feature maps by keeping only the strongest responses in each small region.

Stacking these layers builds up meaning. Early layers find edges, middle layers combine them into shapes like eyes or wheels, and later layers recognise whole objects. A final [[Fully Connected Layer|fully connected layer]] turns the features into a decision, for example "cat" or "dog". The filter values are not designed by hand. They are learned by [[Backpropagation]].
